title: Glucoraphanin and sulforaphane mitigate TNFalpha-induced Caco-2 monolayers permeabilization and inflammation.
authors: Zhu, Wei; Cremonini, Eleonora; Mastaloudis, Angela; Oteiza, Patricia I
one_liner_zh: 研究萝卜硫苷和莱菔硫烷对TNFα诱导的Caco-2细胞屏障通透化的缓解作用，涉及炎症信号通路和分子对接，但无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无结合建模，且方法仅为初步分子对接，与本课题无关。
abstract: Intestinal permeabilization is central to the pathophysiology of chronic gut inflammation. This study investigated the efficacy of glucoraphanin (GR), prevalent in cruciferous vegetables, particularly broccoli, and its derivative sulforaphane (SF), in inhibiting tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNFalpha)-induced Caco-2 cell monolayers inflammation and permeabilization through the regulation of redox-sensitive events. TNFalpha binding to its receptor led to a rapid increase in oxidant production and subsequent elevation in the mRNA levels of NOX1, NOX4, and Duox2. GR and SF dose-dependently mitigated both these short- and long-term alterations in redox homeostasis. Downstream, GR and SF inhibited the activation of the redox-sensitive signaling cascades NF-kappaB (p65 and IKK) and MAPK ERK1/2, which contribute to inflammation and barrier permeabilization. GR (1 muM) and SF (0.5-1 muM) prevented TNFalpha-induced monolayer permeabilization and the associated reduction in the levels of the tight junction (TJ) proteins occludin and ZO-1. Both GR and SF also mitigated TNFalpha-induced increased mRNA levels of the myosin light chain kinase, which promotes TJ opening. Molecular docking suggests that although GR is mostly not absorbed, it could interact with extracellular and membrane sites in NOX1. Inhibition of NOX1 activity by GR would mitigate TNFalpha receptor downstream signaling and associated events. These findings support the concept that not only SF, but also GR, could exert systemic health benefits by protecting the intestinal barrier against inflammation-induced permeabilization, in part by regulating redox-sensitive pathways. GR has heretofore not been viewed as a biologically active molecule, but rather, the benign precursor of highly active SF. The consumption of GR and/or SF-rich vegetables or supplements in the diet may offer a means to mitigate the detrimental consequences of intestinal permeabilization, not only in disease states but also in conditions characterized by chronic inflammation of dietary and lifestyle origin.
abstract_zh: 肠道通透性增加是慢性肠道炎症病理生理学的核心。本研究探讨了 glucoraphanin (GR)（十字花科蔬菜，尤其是西兰花中含量丰富）及其衍生物 sulforaphane (SF) 通过调节氧化还原敏感事件抑制肿瘤坏死因子α (TNFalpha) 诱导的 Caco-2 细胞单层炎症和通透性增加的 efficacy。TNFalpha 与其受体结合导致氧化剂产生迅速增加，随后 NOX1、NOX4 和 Duox2 的 mRNA 水平升高。GR 和 SF 剂量依赖性地缓解了这些短期和长期的氧化还原稳态改变。在下游，GR 和 SF 抑制了氧化还原敏感信号级联 NF-kappaB（p65 和 IKK）和 MAPK ERK1/2 的激活，这些信号通路参与炎症和屏障通透性增加。GR (1 muM) 和 SF (0.5-1 muM) 阻止了 TNFalpha 诱导的单层通透性增加及紧密连接 (TJ) 蛋白 occludin 和 ZO-1 水平的相应降低。GR 和 SF 还缓解了 TNFalpha 诱导的肌球蛋白轻链激酶 mRNA 水平升高，该激酶促进 TJ 开放。分子对接提示，尽管 GR 大部分不被吸收，但它可能与 NOX1 的细胞外和膜位点相互作用。GR 对 NOX1 活性的抑制将缓解 TNFalpha 受体下游信号传导及相关事件。这些发现支持以下概念：不仅 SF，而且 GR 也可能通过保护肠道屏障免受炎症诱导的通透性增加，部分通过调节氧化还原敏感通路，发挥系统性健康益处。GR 迄今未被视为生物活性分子，而是高活性 SF 的良性前体。饮食中摄入富含 GR 和/或 SF 的蔬菜或补充剂可能提供一种缓解肠道通透性增加不良后果的手段，不仅在疾病状态下，而且在以饮食和生活方式来源的慢性炎症为特征的条件下也是如此。
